investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T06:36–06:43Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods unscheduled for 121–146 seconds until the eval timed out. Because the pod never started, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever written, causing a total contract gap.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the only 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable slots and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod is immediately placed in an Unschedulable state. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion on the production Kubernetes cluster, not an eval runner or contract configuration defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885, createAgent call) never receives a running VM, so it cannot populate any of the four required evidence fields.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable scheduler message for a third independently submitted pod (144s stuck), further confirming cluster-wide kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: the cluster has no remaining VM slots for new remote-agent pods. All three sibling checks independently confirm this with the same scheduler rejection reason (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector at all, meaning only 2 nodes are even candidates. If the affinity rules were recently tightened or node labels changed, the effective schedulable pool may have shrunk, accelerating exhaustion.

TERTIARY — leaked or zombie remote-agent VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if prior eval runs or user-created agents were not cleaned up (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs), their VM resource allocations may still be counted against the node capacity, leaving no room for new pods.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — transient cluster event (node eviction, maintenance cordon): one or both of the 2 eligible nodes may have been temporarily cordoned or under pressure at the time of the run, reducing available vm slots to zero for the duration of the eval window.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T06:36–06:43Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods unscheduled for 121–146 seconds until the eval timed out. Because the pod never started, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever written, causing a total contract gap.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the only 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable slots and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod is immediately placed in an Unschedulable state. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion on the production Kubernetes cluster, not an eval runner or contract configuration defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885, createAgent call) never receives a running VM, so it cannot populate any of the four required evidence fields.

All three sibling checks independently confirm this with the same scheduler rejection reason (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector at all, meaning only 2 nodes are even candidates. If the affinity rules were recently tightened or node labels changed, the effective schedulable pool may have shrunk, accelerating exhaustion.

TERTIARY — leaked or zombie remote-agent VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if prior eval runs or user-created agents were not cleaned up (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs), their VM resource allocations may still be counted against the node capacity, leaving no room for new pods.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM workload: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No preemption victims were available, so every pod creation attempt timed out unscheduled and no runtime evidence was ever collected.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm runtime has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the 2 eligible nodes. The pod scheduler reports "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" with no preemption path available. Because the agent pod never scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never completed, no evidence was returned, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (requiring orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure resource constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was stuck unscheduled for 144s before the eval timed out.

sibling.remote-agent-create: identical scheduler error ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'), pod stuck 121s, confirming the resource exhaustion predates the runtime check and affects agent creation as well.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error, pod stuck 146s, confirming the constraint persisted across the full eval window (06:38–06:43 UTC).
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}), confirming the agent pod never reached a running state and no runtime response was captured.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing, consistent with the probe never advancing past createAgent due to scheduling failure.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918 immediately after acquiring orgId — this is the call that would submit the pod and block on scheduling.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false with outageLatencyMs=420000; the eval ran for 146815ms, well within the outage threshold, so the failure is a scheduling timeout, not a latency breach.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote agent pods or other peer-pod workloads are consuming all available VM slots, leaving none for the eval probe pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's affinity/selector rules, artificially constraining the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or stale, the effective capacity is lower than the cluster's total.

Tertiary — insufficient kata peer-pod node capacity in the cluster: the cluster may simply not have enough nodes configured with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource to handle concurrent eval probe pods alongside production workloads.

Lower confidence — transient spike in remote agent creation by real users or other automated processes consuming VM slots at the time of the eval run (no user-traffic evidence is present to confirm or deny this).

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the Kubernetes cluster shows available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different scheduling or admission error would need to be investigated.

If the pod spec for remote agent creation does not request the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, the scheduler message would indicate a different root cause (e.g., a node label mismatch or runtime class misconfiguration).

If re-running the eval immediately after the failure window produces a pass with all 5 required evidence fields present, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief spike in VM slot consumption) rather than a sustained capacity problem.

If the 4 nodes excluded by affinity/selector are actually kata-capable and the selector rules are misconfigured, the root cause would shift from resource exhaustion to affinity misconfiguration, and fixing the selector alone might resolve the issue without adding capacity.

If user-traffic or incident signals show no impact on real remote agent provisioning during the same window, the failure is isolated to the eval probe environment and may reflect a quota or namespace constraint specific to the eval workload.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries the Kubernetes cluster for available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity before attempting remote agent creation, and fails fast with a descriptive capacity-exhaustion message rather than waiting for the scheduler timeout.

Add a dedicated eval check for kata peer-pod node availability that independently verifies the count of schedulable nodes and available VM slots, decoupled from the agent creation flow, so capacity exhaustion is surfaced as its own signal.

Add a historical baseline eval that tracks the pass/fail trend for remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime over time; the current history shows previousRunCount=0 and no lastPassingAt, making regression detection impossible.

Add a sibling-correlation eval rule that automatically flags when all checks under a feature fail with the same scheduler error pattern, to distinguish infrastructure-layer failures from application-layer failures earlier in triage.
